html:
The Ottoman-Wahhabi War was fought from 1811 to 1818 between the first Saudi state, the Emirate of Diriyah, and the army of Egypt, sent by the Ottoman sultan to take back the holy cities.

The Wahhabis had taken Mecca and Medina and stopped the Ottoman pilgrim caravans, a blow to the sultan's standing. Muhammad Ali of Egypt sent his son Tusun, who retook the holy cities by 1813, and then his son Ibrahim Pasha, who marched into Najd. After a siege of months, Diriyah surrendered in September 1818 and was razed.

The Saudi ruler Abdullah bin Saud was sent to Istanbul and beheaded. The family came back within a few years, setting up a second state at Riyadh. See also Ottoman Empire.
